column3: The stock DECLARE_CLASS named NCWnd as the super while the C++ base is NCNPCHtmlViewer (the stock Super:: is NCWnd); our header keeps the C++ base. The generated IMPLEMENT_CLASS takes the super from analysis/classes.json (docs/notas/Standalone.md, section 3).
The stock DECLARE_CLASS named NCWnd as the super while the C++ base is NCItemWnd; same case as NCTestHtmlViewer.

The stock DECLARE_CLASS named NCWnd as the super (classes.json super NCWnd) while the C++ base is NCDialogBox (its constructor 0x1010ca70 calls the NCDialogBox one, 0x1000a130); same case as NCTestHtmlViewer.

The stock DECLARE_CLASS named NCWnd as the super while the C++ base is NCAbnormalStatusWnd (its constructor 0x101135d0 calls the NCAbnormalStatusWnd one, 0x10102710, with icon size 24); same case as NCTestHtmlViewer.

The stock DECLARE_CLASS named NCQuestWnd as the super while the C++ base is NCQuestGaraTreeWnd (its constructor 0x10084fa0 calls the NCQuestGaraTreeWnd one, 0x100dc280); same case as NCTestHtmlViewer. The generated IMPLEMENT_CLASS registers the stock parent.

The stock NCCmdTarget vtable has 39 slots (UObject 25 + NCCmdTarget 14, C3 and C4); ours declares the 25 of the NCObject and NCWnd declares slots 25..38 (src/nwindow/NCWnd.cpp). NW_CHECK_VTABLE compares the 25 that exist.

Our NCCmdTarget declares no virtual of its own (25 slots, the NCObject ones), the stock 39 (slots 25..38 are declared in NCWnd here). NCCmdTarget is abstract and only NCWnd derives from it: its vtable is live only inside NCCmdTarget's constructor and destructor, which call no slot above 24.
The stock image emitted appMemcpy out of line (0x10001790) with an SSE branch on Core's GIsSSE; the standalone build has the C runtime's memcpy. Nothing else of the game code reads it.
Only the stock NL2Font constructor (0x1005b7a0) stores the intermediate FExec vtable (Core's) before its own; ours does not store it (docs/notas/Standalone.md, section 10).

Slot 68 (GetValue): the stock slot is the 8-byte body 0x100faac0 (`mov eax,[ecx]; jmp [eax+0x114]`, a tail jump into the object's slot 69, CommitText for an edit box), which the db names NCPlayerStatusWnd::Resize (the linker folded the two: Resize also tail-jumps into slot 69, OnResize). Ours is NCHtmlEdit::GetValue `return CommitText();`, the same virtual call; aliasing the slot to our Resize would rely on the compiler emitting Resize(INT) as a bare tail jump (sa-win-a).
Slot 68 (GetValue): the same shared tail-jump body 0x100faac0 as NCHtmlEdit's slot 68 (see that note); ours is NCJHtmlEdit::GetValue `return CommitText();` (sa-win-a).

Core's FString(INT, INT) only stores three zero dwords (an empty string). The C3 stock's game code calls it as FString(0, 1) (push 1; push 0 before call [0x101750b4]) for the empty result of a failed lookup in two functions: NChatHeaderMap::Lookup (0x101279c0, at 0x10127a1f) and NMsnIntStrMap::FindRef (0x1013e1c0, at 0x1013e203). Ours returns `FString()` in both (ChatWnd.cpp, NotificationProcess.cpp), Core's default constructor, which this DLL imports: the same three zero stores (as C4's note; sa-integ read the C3 calls).

Core's FString(const char*) builds the wide string of a narrow one. The C3 stock calls it (call [0x101750b8]) in nine functions, each with an ASCII literal pushed just before: MsnCommand::ToString 0x10127420 " ", NMsnGroup::SetName 0x1012dbd0 " " and "%20", NChatSbSender::SendTyping 0x1012e3e0 "U", NChatSbSender::SendText 0x1012e4d0 "N", SwitchboardSession::SendMSG 0x1012e5c0 "N", NChatSbSender::SendInvite 0x1012e6b0 "CAL", SwitchboardSession::AddFriend 0x1012e8e0 "NLN", NChatNotifySender::RequestSwitchboard 0x1013fef0 "XFR" and "SB", NotificationProcess::OnAsyncImpl 0x10140a20 "FLN". Ours builds the same texts with the wide constructor FString(const TCHAR*) from the same ASCII literals (identity conversion, the same Num = Max = length + 1). (SetName passes its two texts to the replacer in the other order than the stock: an open decision of sa-integ's report, not an import question.)

Core's FString::InStr(const FString&, INT) is a thunk that loads the string's data pointer (or Core's static empty text) and tail-jumps to InStr(const TCHAR*, INT). The C3 stock's NMsnStrReplaceImpl (0x10143ed0) calls it twice (at 0x10143f34 and 0x10143fd7, Right = 0); ours calls `Str->InStr(*From, 0)` at both places (ChatWnd.cpp), the TCHAR* overload this DLL imports, with the same data pointer: the same call.

The C3 stock's NConsoleWnd::Initialize (0x10077f20) loads GIsL2NetLogin and compares it with 0 at 0x10078a3c..0x10078a42, then jumps unconditionally (0x10078a45 jmp 0x10078a52: the packager's patch): the result of the compare is never used and the skipped branch is the GameGuard start (NConsoleWnd::StartGameGuard, out of the standalone by the owner's decision). Ours does not read it (NConsoleWndWindows.cpp): nothing is lost.
